title: Tenali Raman and the Heavy Bundle on the Cart

full_text:
While traveling across the countryside toward Hampi, Tenali Raman sat comfortably in his bullock cart, driven by a faithful servant. Along the dusty, sun-baked highway, Tenali noticed a weary traveler walking with bent shoulders, carrying an enormous, heavy sack of wheat upon his head. The man was sweating profusely, groaning with every step.

Moved by compassion, Tenali stopped the cart:
'Brother, thou art weary. Climb into my cart; we are traveling to the same city.'

The traveler thanked Tenali with tears of relief, climbed into the back of the wooden cart, and sat down upon the straw.
However, Tenali noticed that the man did not put down the heavy sack of wheat!
He continued balancing the massive sack upon his aching head, his neck muscles straining, sweat pouring into his eyes, gripping the burlap bag with both hands!

Tenali looked back in utter astonishment:
'Friend! Why art thou still carrying that heavy sack upon thy head?
Put it down upon the floor of the cart!'

The traveler replied with earnest, simple-minded concern:
'Noble master, you have been so kind to let me ride in your cart.
Your two bullocks are already pulling the weight of the cart, your servant, and myself.
I did not want to burden your poor bullocks with the extra weight of my heavy sack of wheat, so I decided to carry it upon my own head!'

Tenali Raman burst into gentle, affectionate laughter:
'O simple brother! Think for a moment!
Where art thou sitting?'
'In the cart, master.'
'And where is the cart resting?'
'Upon its wheels.'
'And who is pulling the cart and everything inside it?'
'The bullocks, master.'

Tenali smiled with deep philosophical warmth:
'Whether the sack rests upon the cart floor or upon thy head, the poor bullocks carry the exact same weight!
The only difference is that by keeping it on thy head, thou art breaking thy own neck for nothing!
Put down thy burden, rest thy weary back, and let the cart carry the load.'

The traveler realized the simple truth, placed the sack upon the straw, and breathed a deep sigh of relief.
Tenali turned to his servant and said:
'Look at human nature! We ride in the great cart of divine destiny, yet we carry the heavy sacks of our anxieties, worries, and fears upon our own heads, sweating and groaning, forgetting that the universe carries both us and our burdens together!'
moral: Worrying endlessly while carried by destiny is like carrying your luggage on your head while riding a bullock cart.
